item.title: Ahead of the US midterms, Gen Z investors are making portfolio changes
item.description: Brandon Gaw is monitoring the news to adjust investments that he thinks could be hit hard by pre-election volatility ahead of the US midterms.
item.dc:creator: Hani Richter
item.content:encoded: Brandon Gaw, an Oregon-based engineering student and investor. Courtesy Brandon Gaw/Handout via REUTERS Brandon Gaw, an Oregon-based engineering student and investor, isn't just watching the news to stay in the know. He's also monitoring it to adjust investments that he thinks could be hit hard by pre-election volatility ahead of the US midterms . “When others are fearful, that's the best time to invest,” he says. One issue the 22-year-old is watching closely is the prospect of tighter restrictions involving Chinese-made memory chips entering the US market, as well as increased competition. Against this backdrop, Gaw says he is holding more cash and selling shares in smaller and newer companies that are more dependent on investors' excitement about AI, which he believes could be especially vulnerable to election uncertainty. Every few weeks, Gaw trades stocks worth $5,000 to $10,000. “In my opinion, those are going to get hit the most,” he says. Brandon Gaw, an Oregon-based engineering student and investor. Courtesy Brandon Gaw/Handout via REUTERS Gaw accepts he’s taking more risk because of his age compared to an investor who may need their money sooner for retirement or a house. But he’s also investing in more established companies, including Microsoft, Google, Nvidia and Apple. “If anything, I added a few more positions in those companies,” he says. “I don't think they're going to run out of business anytime soon.” For now, Gaw’s portfolio is fairly spread out: crypto, gold and silver collectively account for about 5% to 10%; ETFs make up around 30%; and individual stocks account for 60%. He has not made changes to his retirement investments. Taking a long-term view, Gaw says a market dip does not matter much to him if the S&P 500 falls. “I think these pullbacks are pretty good buying opportunities,” he says. THE WIDER TREND Nearly three-quarters of Gen Z investors have changed their retirement savings or portfolios in anticipation of the midterm election outcomes, compared to just 17% of Baby Boomers, according to a recent Nationwide Retirement Institute survey of over 2,000 US investors. Tyler McConville, a Wisconsin-based certified financial planner and private wealth advisor at Capital Group, says “The challenge is determining which information actually matters to a long-term financial plan.” While it is important to pay attention to elections and policy changes, markets have historically been influenced more by economic fundamentals and specific policy outcomes. “The biggest risk is when investors make long-term portfolio decisions based on short-term political concerns,” he says. KEY TAKEAWAYS Don’t make speculative trades. Use market-moving events as a reminder to review your investments and to consider how elections could affect certain sectors. Keep diversification in mind. Gaw spreads his investments across individual stocks, ETFs, crypto and precious metals, while reducing his exposure to stocks that he considers volatile. A diversified portfolio can help limit reliance on any one investment or sector. Focus on economic fundamentals. Rather than assuming one political party will be good or bad for stocks, consider factors such as inflation, interest rates, corporate earnings and specific policy changes when assessing your investments. Have a money lesson or story to share? Tell us what worked for you — or what didn’t — by emailing hani.richter@tr.com .

item.title: Japan to arrange private investments worth $6.36 billion in Bangladesh, Nikkei reports
item.description: Japan will agree to arrange 1 trillion yen ($6.36 billion) in private-sector investments in Bangladesh over the next five years, the Nikkei newspaper reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan will agree to arrange 1 trillion yen ($6.36 billion) in private-sector investments in Bangladesh over the next five years, the Nikkei newspaper reported on Thursday. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will host her Bangladesh counterpart Tarique Rahman for a summit in Japan this month, and a joint statement will mention the arrangement, the report said. The investments are expected to go into automobile and other manufacturing industries, as well as the construction of energy facilities, Nikkei reported. It will also involve companies entering the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone being developed by parties including Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp (8053.T) , the newspaper added. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. ($1 = 157.1900 yen)

Cable capacity emerges as bottleneck for AI data centres, Nexans says

FAST

Oct 22 : Cable production capacity is emerging as a bottleneck for AI-driven data centre construction, Nexans' finance chief said, as demand rises faster than the industry's ability to expand manufacturing capacity. Global cable capacity is tight and building a new cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable production line, known in the industry as a CV line, takes around three years, limiting how quickly suppliers can respond to demand, Nexans CFO Vincent Piquet told Reuters. "Things can't move quickly and the people building these data centres are in a great hurry," Piquet said. Data centres require large amounts of low- and medium-voltage cable to connect power infrastructure, with larger facilities consuming proportionately more medium-voltage cable.

The strain on power infrastructure is already delaying some projects. In September, Oracle issued a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl unit developing a large data centre in New Mexico, citing potential difficulties securing sufficient power for the site. Piquet said grid constraints, while slowing some projects, were also supporting demand for Nexans' products and allowing the company to be more selective when allocating capacity. French distribution network operator Enedis has moved from annual procurement agreements to contracts lasting six or seven years in order to secure cable supply, he said. While Europe generally faces fewer grid-connection challenges than the United States and benefits from stronger electricity networks in some northern countries, Piquet said lengthy regulatory processes were delaying certain projects. He said he did not expect demand linked to artificial intelligence to slow, although Europe's data-centre expansion was likely to be less pronounced than in the United States because private investment capacity was smaller and public funding played a larger role.

item.title: South Africa’s Trade With China Surges After Beijing’s Zero-Tariff Deal
item.description: South Africa’s trade with China has increased since Beijing introduced a temporary zero-tariff scheme for qualifying South African exports in May, offering Pretoria an opportunity to expand sales to its largest trading partner as relations with the United States come under increasing strain. South African …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
South Africa’s trade with China has increased since Beijing introduced a temporary zero-tariff scheme for qualifying South African exports in May, offering Pretoria an opportunity to expand sales to its largest trading partner as relations with the United States come under increasing strain.

South African exports to China rose nearly 25% year over year between May and August, while imports from China increased 23% over the same period, Chinese Ambassador Wu Peng said at an event in Pretoria on Thursday.

South Africa has been seeking to rebalance its trade with China, which is its largest trading partner. In 2025, South Africa exported about 222 billion rand ($13.5 billion) worth of goods to China and imported nearly twice that amount, Trade Minister Parks Tau said.

South Africa’s exports to China include agricultural products, minerals and manufactured goods. The government is seeking to expand access for higher-value products as it looks to narrow the trade imbalance and diversify its export markets.

Wu said he had heard South Africa’s concerns about the imbalance in bilateral trade and expressed confidence that Chinese market access for South African products would expand.

“I am confident more and more South African high value-added products will enter the Chinese market in the future,” he said.

China’s zero-tariff preference scheme took effect on May 1, 2026, and is scheduled to run through April 30, 2028, pending a broader economic partnership arrangement between China and African countries. The temporary measure covers qualifying South African exports that meet applicable rules of origin and documentation requirements, while certain products are subject to tariff-rate quotas.

The arrangement provides South African exporters with an opportunity to compete in the Chinese market without paying customs duties on eligible goods. However, the increase in trade recorded since May does not establish how much of the growth resulted directly from the tariff changes.

For Pretoria, expanding exports to China is part of a broader effort to develop alternative markets as uncertainty over access to the U.S. market threatens an established source of export demand.

The United States has extended the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which gives eligible sub-Saharan African countries duty-free access to the U.S. market for thousands of products, through 2028. South Africa, however, faces the risk of exclusion as President Donald Trump’s administration has criticized several of its domestic and foreign policies.

The Trump administration has accused the South African government of persecuting white people, an allegation Pretoria denies.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said on October 19 that the country must prepare for the possibility of losing its AGOA benefits, as his government pursues alternative markets and holds discussions with U.S. counterparts.

Tau said he expected an announcement in early November on whether South Africa would be excluded from the program, but remained “cautiously optimistic.”

The uncertainty has added urgency to South Africa’s efforts to diversify its export destinations, including through stronger commercial ties with China. However, expanding trade with Beijing does not necessarily guarantee a reduction in the bilateral trade imbalance, particularly as imports from China are also rising.

South Africa’s ability to benefit from the Chinese scheme will depend partly on whether domestic producers can increase exports of qualifying goods and move into higher-value agricultural, industrial and processed products. The tariff preference removes customs duties on eligible exports but does not eliminate other market-access requirements.

The two countries’ trade figures point to expanding commercial ties, but the challenge for Pretoria will be to translate that growth into greater export earnings and a more balanced trading relationship.

With a decision on South Africa’s AGOA eligibility expected in early November, the country faces pressure to strengthen its position in China and other markets while seeking to preserve preferential access to the United States.

item.title: Anthropic IPO stands alone as AI market jitters sideline others
item.description: A once-robust fall calendar for technology IPOs is down to just Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wang
item.content:encoded: A once-robust fall calendar for technology IPOs is down to just Anthropic. The AI lab is pressing ahead to hold its initial public offering as planned in the middle of next month after making its prospectus public as early as late October, people familiar with the matter said, cautioning the plan and the dates are subject to change. Anthropic's planned IPO will test whether its position at the center of the booming AI business, which some investors believe to deem worthy of a potential $1.5 trillion valuation, can overcome a market environment that might typically prompt bankers and deal lawyers to counsel delay. Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its shares to prospective investors during the week of November 9, one of the people said. Other companies in the artificial intelligence infrastructure and data center sectors have delayed their listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending. The contrast underscores Anthropic's appeal to investors even as concerns about competition from open-source models and AI safety weigh on the sector. Many large investors remain bullish on Anthropic’s prospects despite the fall turbulence, viewing the firm as one of the few opportunities to gain exposure to a technology sector that long-term investors cannot afford to ignore. Other issuers are reluctant to compete with Anthropic for institutional investors' attention and capital, two of the people said. Anthropic declined to comment. VALUATIONS COMING UNDER PRESSURE The AI sector pullback follows a string of IPO delays and withdrawals since September, as market volatility and rising interest rates have made it harder for companies to secure attractive valuations. Switch, a data center operator, and Nscale, an AI infrastructure provider, have pushed their IPO plans back to later this year, people familiar with the matter said, while stressing that plans remain fluid and subject to change. Nscale’s delay was partly driven by the need to address comments from SEC staff, one other person said. SoftBank-backed SB Energy has also postponed its listing, Reuters previously reported. NScale declined to comment. Switch didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Blackstone-backed [USN:L6N45Z09R TEXT:"AirTrunk REIT"] and Nvidia (NVDA.O) -backed [USN:P8N42P0IJ TEXT:"Firmus"] have pulled or paused their offerings, Reuters has reported. Oura's recent IPO has added to the caution among prospective issuers. The offering attracted little participation from long-only investors, a person familiar with the matter said, raising concerns about the depth of demand from institutional investors that typically provide a stable base of shareholders for newly listed companies. SCRUTINY ON MULTIPLE FRONTS The retreat from AI infrastructure listings reflects growing scrutiny of the enormous capital required to build data centers and whether future demand will justify the investment. Recent developments involving CoreWeave have added to concerns about a potential slowdown in AI spending, although some market participants do not expect such a downturn to materialize. Nscale publicly filed its IPO registration statement in September, while Switch submitted its filing confidentially, Reuters reported previously. A confidential filing allows a company to work with regulators on its registration statement before disclosing financial and business details to the public. Companies typically publish the filing ahead of investor roadshows, when they begin marketing shares to prospective investors.

item.title: Will US Treasury scrap 20-year bond sales?
item.description: The US Treasury's auction of 20-year bonds on Wednesday won’t be the last, but this long-term debt instrument's days may be numbered.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: The US Treasury's auction of 20-year bonds on Wednesday won’t be the last, but this long-term debt instrument's days may be numbered. Long-term borrowing costs are high. Yields on 10-year and 30-year Treasuries earlier this month rose to their highest levels since 2002, reaching 5.36% and 5.66%, respectively. The 5.469% that Treasury paid to borrow $13 billion on Wednesday was the highest yield at a 20-year auction since 1986. Discussion of whether the government should scrap this less liquid maturity altogether has intensified recently. Meanwhile, US federal debt has crossed the $40 trillion threshold, while Washington's interest bill for fiscal 2026 hit a record $1.36 trillion, putting interest payments as a share of GDP at a historic high of 3.2%. These metrics are all rising. When debt is above $40 trillion, a few basis points lower in borrowing costs can save billions. This points to an obvious strategy for lowering average government borrowing costs: lighten the load at the long end of the curve and borrow more at the front, where rates are lower. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appears intent on doing just that. In August, Treasury announced it would at least double its $2 billion scheduled buybacks of longer-dated debt, referring to 10-year notes and 20- and 30-year bonds. It later increased that to $6 billion. Treasury said this reflected its "desire to provide greater liquidity support" to certain parts of the curve. That may be true, but it also just happens to align with longer-term efforts to shorten Treasury’s maturity profile. Around 22% of US public debt is currently in T-bills, which mature in one year or less, compared with around 15% five years ago. This is far from a “risk-free” strategy. By increasing the share of short-term debt, the government gives up the security of longer-term financing, meaning it must refinance more often. This "rollover risk" exposes the government to bouts of market shocks or volatility. But Bessent has few options. DEAR PRUDENCE A sudden burst of deficit-reduction fervor could sweep across Washington, leading to huge spending cuts or large tax hikes. But that's unlikely. The US budget deficit hit $2 trillion in fiscal 2026, more than 6% of GDP, and there is little appetite in the White House to tackle it. President Donald Trump recently pledged to mail $5,000 checks to every adult in the country if his Republican Party wins both houses of Congress in the midterm elections on November 3, a splurge that would cost over $1.1 trillion, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget. Absent serious belt-tightening, Treasury has to consider other measures to help lower long-term borrowing costs. One could be reducing sales of the 20-year bond or getting rid of it entirely. The 20-year is one of the least liquid parts of the yield curve, with a limited supply of natural buyers. That means the government often has to offer a slightly more attractive yield. Markets will find out more in the first week of November when Treasury unveils its quarterly refunding plans. What can we expect? Normally, very little. In the words of the Treasury itself, the debt auction process, calendar and issuance amounts should be “regular and predictable” to ensure smooth functioning of the world's largest and most important market. But these are not normal times. The Treasury’s $6 billion accelerated buyback plan proved to be a bit of a flop, as the government failed to purchase the full amount in the first two rounds of buybacks in September. More importantly, long-dated yields rose as much as 50 basis points following the buyback announcement. Citi's US rates strategists expect 20-year and 30-year auction sizes to be reduced by $3 billion, with the gap filled by additional bill issuance. Treasury may also opt for more flexibility by keeping auction sizes unchanged but signaling that future adjustments are in play. Alternatively, Treasury may decide to retain the status quo. Analysts at JPMorgan reckon the scale of borrowing required in the coming years is so huge that it would "not be prudent" to discontinue a "critical" source of funding from an instrument that raises $168 billion a year. What's more, yields might be high, but they're not disconnected from current economic fundamentals, they argue. Given that the midterm elections are also in the first week of November, Treasury’s quarterly refunding plan may not be absolutely top of mind for investors. But that might be a mistake, as subtle changes in the government’s funding strategy could have big implications down the line. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. Follow ROI on LinkedIn, and X. And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple, Spotify, or the Reuters app. Subscribe to hear Reuters journalists discuss the biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.

item.title: Tesla drops as spending pullback clouds AI, robotics ambitions
item.description: Tesla’s shares slid five per cent in premarket trading on Thursday as the EV maker’s reduced capital spending forecast raised questions about the pace of investment behind Elon Musk’s AI, robotics and ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Tesla’s shares slid five per cent in premarket trading on Thursday as the EV maker’s reduced capital spending forecast raised questions about the pace of investment behind Elon Musk’s AI, robotics and autonomous-driving ambitions. The company on Wednesday lowered its 2026 capital spending forecast to about US$20 billion from more than $25 billion after spending far less than expected on AI and robotics in the third quarter, which led to a surprise positive free cash flow. The strong position may prove valuable as CEO Musk explores combining Tesla with the far more capital-intensive SpaceX. But “investors are likely to come away with mixed feelings,” J.P.Morgan analysts, led by Rajat Gupta, wrote in a note. “The delay helps near-term cash burn but also suggests delays in investments that matter for fruition of long-term opportunities.” Wednesday’s management commentary suggested spending will be ramped up in 2027 and 2028 as Tesla continues to fund robotaxi, Optimus, AI compute and Terafab milestones, the brokerage said. Tesla’s shares have declined about 14 per cent this year, in contrast to the Nasdaq’s roughly 15 per cent gain. The stock is about 23 per cent below its record intraday high of $498.83, reached in December 2025. Its valuation, however, remains well above peers: Tesla traded at 188.24 times its forward earnings estimates, compared with 6.58 for Ford and 5.16 for General Motors. “The risk is Tesla now enters a period of limbo while investors await news on a potential combination with SpaceX, which ... might face significant regulatory hurdles,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell. (Reporting by Joel Jose in Bengaluru; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

item.title: Ambani's heir Akash steps into the spotlight as India's Jio goes public
item.description: In Asia's richest family that controls the oil-to-retail Reliance empire, Mukesh Ambani's eldest son Akash is set to take centre stage as their telecoms and digital unit nears a stock market debut.
item.dc:creator: Vibhuti Sharma
item.content:encoded: In Asia's richest family that controls the oil-to-retail Reliance empire, Mukesh Ambani's eldest son Akash is set to take centre stage as their telecoms and digital unit nears a stock market debut. Akash Ambani, who turned 35 on Friday, is the managing director of Jio Platforms, whose $3.2 billion IPO this week was [USN:L4N46512K TEXT:"fully subscribed"] within two hours of opening for public bidding, a rare feat for an Indian offering of this size. Though Ambani senior still chairs the holding company Jio Platforms, Akash was anointed chairman of its money-spinning telecoms unit in 2022, in what was widely seen as part of the billionaire’s succession planning. In a sign of his growing clout, Akash led the pitch at Jio Platforms' IPO event last week where he briefed about the company's 533 million customers and profit margins. While his twin sister shared the stage, their father skipped the event. "I’m here as a representative of the entire company," he said. Industry executives who work with Akash described him as an extremely approachable executive who is very hands-on with technology. While Akash weighs in on "some of the bigger calls", he doesn't interfere in day-to-day business decisions. But he does deal with their most marquee investors including Meta, said one executive, who has worked closely on the IPO and with Akash. "He is the one who makes the calls to Mark Zuckerberg," the executive added. Meta is among Jio's largest shareholders with a near 10% stake. In 2020, it joined Google and other global investors in putting 1.52 trillion rupees into the company, worth $20.5 billion at the time. However, Akash and his father -- who are both night owls -- manage investor relationships separately, the industry executive said. Mukesh is closer to many sovereign wealth funds, while his son takes the position as Reliance's Silicon Valley man. Reliance and Meta did not respond to Reuters queries. CREATING THE RELIANCE BRAND Akash holds a bachelor’s in Economics from Brown University in the US and, as an avid sports enthusiast, plays a key role in the management of an Indian Premier League cricket franchise. Married in 2019, he has two children. By Thursday, the IPO’s retail portion was [USN:L1N46807C TEXT:"fully subscribed"], the employee quota drew bids for nearly twice the shares on offer and the existing Reliance shareholders quota was 2.58 times subscribed, exchange data showed. That interest from small investors is reminiscent of how Akash's grandfather Dhirubhai Ambani, who died in 2002, built Reliance's brand image with shareholders, holding large-scale meets in Mumbai’s open grounds in the 1980s that turned Reliance into a company that helps create long-term wealth. The conglomerate's Mumbai listed shares — that have a current market capitalization of $172 billion — have risen 330-fold since 1990. As Akash spoke at the event last week, a garlanded portrait of a smiling Dhirubhai was propped on an easel, while the screen showed black-and-white photos of old shareholder meets. JUST A TELCO? Jio's telecoms business was launched in 2016 and disrupted the market by offering free voice and data. Today, on the basis of customers in a single country, Jio's 500 million-plus users are second only to China Mobile (600941.SS) . Jio Platforms says Akash is leading its long-term "strategic roadmap to transform connectivity and digital services in India" from 4G to 5G and now AI. The company offers apps, digital services and home devices, but telecoms still brings in nearly 90% of its $15.45 billion revenue and around 94% of its profit. Akash and Jio appear keen to dispel the notion that Jio is just a telecoms company. The first line of the company overview in its prospectus reads: "We are a technology platform." Asked about rivalry with Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea, Akash told the Business Standard newspaper recently that "Jio is not just a telco," but a digital services company built on connectivity. At last week's event, he talked up plans to offer AI-powered call summaries and transcription in 12 Indian languages to Jio’s users, saying, "We’re the only play in town that can do that." "What we have is an innate understanding of our Jio customers," he said.

item.title: US banks are blocking third-party AI agents access to customer accounts, sources say
item.description: They are increasingly concerned sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Major US banks have been blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts and making transactions, two people familiar with the situation said, following a report that AI agents were accessing bank accounts and taking actions independent of user instructions. The banking industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. An Axios report on Thursday said some AI agents attempted to take actions that appeared to be independent of user instructions, citing people familiar with the matter. In some cases, bank customers have shared their login ID and password with agents, with banks typically flagging and blocking those transactions, a person in the banking industry said. Still, such transactions cannot be deemed unauthorized if credentials were shared by the customer. Morgan Stanley (MS.N) has blocked third-party agents from accessing its platforms, but it had not seen any instances of unauthorized or rogue AI agents, according to a person familiar with the matter. Top banking executives earlier this month [USN:L4N45Z1M8 TEXT:"discussed the risks of AI agents"] acting on customers' behalf, with some warning the technology is adding significant risks for both customers and banks. JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) CEO Jamie Dimon earlier this month said the largest US lender was developing tools to navigate the risk of AI agents carrying out tasks on their own. "We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," he said at the time. Charles Schwab (SCHW.N) CEO Richard Wurster earlier this month also said the brokerage was blocking unauthorized agents. "I get a report every day tracking how many times we've had to block one of the different agents, and it's not many because I think people aren't using it in that way in their financial life. We are blocking it because we want to have control over authentication and the experience," Wurster said.

item.title: Meta's AI bill
item.description: Meta shares rise after an earnings beat and excitement around its new Muse AI agent, even as the company burns cash and plans a new share sale.

item.description: US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only".
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes

US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only".

Buildings along King Fahd Road in the Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on Oct 14, 2026. (Photo: AP/Baraa Anwer)

FAST

JERUSALEM: The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters. The order came as attacks in Saudi Arabia killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam and two people were killed in a drone attack on an oil field. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a post on X that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only" amid attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen on civilian targets in the country. Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months after many were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities after the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott said.

Related:

UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi from Houthi attacks

Singaporeans advised to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia amid heightened security risks: MFA

Four US officials told Reuters that US missions in other Gulf states would also be ordering family members to leave. Pigott did not address changes to other missions outside Saudi Arabia. The latest withdrawals follow an escalation of the fighting in Yemen, opening another front in the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The wider conflict has snarled global energy trade and hurt Gulf economies. After the departure order, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority reported an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight others. Earlier in the day, two people were killed after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, the energy ministry said. The US embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on Wednesday (Oct 21) about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia, after recent deadly strikes including on Riyadh's airport. The embassy and a CIA station hosted there came under attack by drones in early March, as Iran began launching attacks across the region.

Cloud services firm Cloudflare saw millions of exploitation attempts after the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language PHP , CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday.  "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it. That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now," Prince said.  Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of vulnerabilities in PHP sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems. Japanese lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group said it was temporarily suspending some internet services due to emergency measures.  Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes to vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years until they were uncovered using AI, saying all users were "encouraged to update immediately." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also urged website owners on Wednesday to check whether their sites use PHP and prepare to apply the new fix.  Japan's Finance Ministry also temporarily suspended some website content and services while security measures were being implemented.

item.title: Hacking attempts surge as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
item.description: Global firms and governments rushed to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista, Toby Sterling, Mariko Katsumura
item.content:encoded: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the [USN:L6N467127 TEXT:"PHP"] programming language that underpins much of the internet, as cloud firms reported a surge of hacking attempts after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. The push came after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites [USN:L6N4670DM TEXT:"offline"] as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to [USN:L6N467188 TEXT:"Helsinki"] mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand. "I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft (MSFT.O) CEO Satya Nadella said at an event in Germany on Thursday, saying the incident showed the importance of building software that can be maintained securely as systems grow more complex. "It was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks." PHP KEY TO INTERNET'S FOUNDATIONS LIKE HTML, PYTHON The developers of PHP - a computing language like HTML and Python - released [USN:L6N4670ZW TEXT:"fixes"] on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI. They urged users to "update immediately". Madeline Lawrence, co-founder of Belgian cybersecurity firm Aikido Security, said that details of the flaws had become public before fixes were ready, with attacks reported since. "Companies are racing to update against attackers who can use AI to exploit them. That's the whole race," she said. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare (NET.N) and Amazon (AMZN.O) . "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday. "That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now." Amazon also said it saw widespread exploitation . IMPACT FROM JAPAN TO FINLAND Japanese companies including brokerage Nomura (8604.T) , lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (8306.T) , airline ANA (9202.T) and East Japan Railway (9020.T) said on Thursday they were temporarily suspending some internet services as part of emergency measures. Brewer Asahi Group Holdings (2502.T) temporarily suspended certain websites and systems and was conducting a security impact assessment. Insurer Tokio Marine Holdings (8766.T) said it had suspended its group website. Japan's Ministry of Finance and Meteorological Agency partially suspended online services to implement safety measures, while Japan's National Tax Agency temporarily took down its service. The precautionary shutdowns show Japan's growing concerns over cybersecurity, as the country [USN:L1N45U0IU TEXT:"recorded"] more cyber incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI. French telecoms group Orange (ORAN.PA) said it had temporarily suspended access to certain PHP-based websites and applications across several subsidiaries as a precaution. Tencent Cloud, one of China's largest cloud-computing providers, urged customers to install updated PHP versions but stopped short of calling for widespread website shutdowns. Finland's state IT services provider Valtori said it had continued installing PHP security patches overnight and was gradually lifting precautionary service blocks after [USN:S8N3WF054 TEXT:"shutting down"] government public web services a day earlier. "Restoring services can take days or even weeks, as in addition to updates, the systems need to be carefully tested," Valtori Director General Hannu Naumanen said in a statement. Valtori said the outages were not caused by exploitation of the vulnerabilities or by a cyber breach, and that it was not aware of any active exploitation of the flaws. SOME FIXES MAY TAKE WEEKS TO IMPLEMENT Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections related to the PHP vulnerabilities on Thursday. China's industry ministry urged organizations and users to inspect systems and upgrade to the latest secure version of PHP. It also recommended strengthening cybersecurity monitoring and changing accounts, passwords and keys where necessary. South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency response measures, citing concerns over an increased risk of hacking attacks. Felix Kuhlenkamp, head of security at German digital industry association Bitkom, said that many larger operators had already carried out updates, but that for complex IT systems and smaller organizations it could take longer. "They may run a website using PHP but don't really keep a close eye on it," he said. "If a website is based on an old version of PHP for which there is no security update, the entire system must be updated."

FAST

ANKARA: Türkiye, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday (Oct 21) to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said. In a statement, the ministry said the countries signed the Badr Memorandum of Understanding in Doha as a sign of their desire to further deepen cooperation and develop partnerships. "The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development. "By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defence industrial capacities, and enable the fulfilment of the needs of allied and friendly nations," it added.

Türkiye, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has been helping Gulf nations, including Qatar, where it has a military base, bolster their defences amid the Iran war. In August, it signed a mutual defence pact with nuclear-armed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, under which an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all. Ankara also has close ties with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry. The ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives. Haluk Gorgun, the chairman of Türkiye's Defence Industry Presidency, said the accord formed the foundation of a "strategic cooperation" to develop joint production and technology. "Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of sustainable defence industry. As Türkiye, we value partnerships that go beyond off-the-shelf procurement models, that foster the development of a nation’s own human capital and industrial infrastructure," Gorgun said in a statement. "We believe that the Badr Memorandum of Understanding will contribute to transforming the complementary capabilities of Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Türkiye into concrete projects," he added.

item.title: Early mailing of Maricopa County ballots does not invalidate them, officials say
item.description: A vendor's mistake caused 3,126 ballots for Maricopa County, Arizona, residents to be mailed six days early, prompting accusations of wrongdoing. Maricopa election officials say the ballots remain valid.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A vendor's mistake caused 3,126 ballots for Maricopa County, Arizona, residents to be mailed six days early, prompting accusations of wrongdoing. Maricopa election officials say the ballots remain valid. Here are the key details: Posts online shared a clip of President Donald Trump saying, “Maricopa sent out thousands of ballots illegally and they got caught and now they’re saying it was an error.” Captions on the post quote Trump’s comments, “it’s crooked” and “Maricopa is a very, very dishonest county,” adding that Maricopa needs to be closely watched in the upcoming November midterms. The Maricopa County Recorder’s Office said in an October 4 press release that the county’s vendor, ballot printer Runbeck Election Services, had mistakenly mailed 3,126 early midterm election ballots on October 1, days before the scheduled October 7 start of mailing and early voting. “Runbeck's error affected only the timing of the mailing. The correct ballots were mailed to the correct voters,” the county’s statement said, adding that the Maricopa County Attorney's Office determined the ballots remain valid. In a statement released on October 4, Runbeck said a pallet of ballots, held apart because they needed non-automated postal handling, was mistakenly released with other mail. It said the ballots were valid, produced from authorized voter data and were sent to the voters who requested them. While it did not authorize the early mailing, the Recorder's Office said the ballots themselves were correct. Arizona law does not address accidental early mailing. Arizona Revised Statute 16-542, section C states that if the Recorder’s office or other election officers receive a request for a mail ballot more than 31 days before election day, it should mail the ballot no earlier than 27 days and no later than 24 days before the election. The Recorder's Office Communications Director, Judy Keane, referred Reuters to the published statements from the office and Runbeck. Verdict: Missing context. The ballots did go out early due to a vendor error and officials say the ballots are valid. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Businesses and investors of Ambani's Jio, which has launched its IPO
item.description: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms is raising up to $3.2 billion in India's largest-ever IPO, valuing the mainly telecoms group at as much as $108.3 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms (JIOP.NS) [USN:L1N467028 TEXT:"is raising"] up to $3.2 billion in India's largest-ever IPO, valuing the mainly telecoms group at as much as $108.3 billion. The IPO was fully subscribed in less than two hours of public bidding this week, in what is a test of investor appetite for the first public offering from the Reliance (RELI.NS) group since in 2006. Here are facts and numbers on Jio Platforms, which counts Meta (META.O) and Google among its major foreign investors: TELECOMS BUSINESS Reliance Jio Platforms is a unit of Ambani's oil-to-retail conglomerate Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) . It is best known for the telecom business Reliance Jio Infocomm, which is the country's biggest player with more than 500 million subscribers. Launched in 2016, the telecom business, popularly referred to simply as Jio, hit rivals such as Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and Vodafone Idea (VODA.NS) hard by offering free voice and data plans initially. The move, in line with Ambani's [USN:L4N35S18O TEXT:"typical strategy"] of offering ultra-low prices to lure consumers, drove up its customer base and allowed many Indians to access platforms such as YouTube and Facebook for the first time. Jio says it currently has a roughly 60% share of India's data traffic. In recent years, Jio Platforms has diversified beyond the telecom sector into AI, cloud and enterprise network services, as well as app development. In 2023, Nvidia (NVDA.O) announced an AI [USN:L1N3AK0MB TEXT:"partnership"] with Reliance to develop cloud infrastructure and language models. THE LEADERSHIP Mukesh Ambani, one of Asia's richest men, is the chairman of Jio Platforms. His three children — [USN:L4N4670YX TEXT:"Akash"], Anant and Isha — serve on its board. Akash Ambani, his elder son, is the chairman of the company's flagship telecom unit, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Reliance Industries holds a 66.43% stake in Jio Platforms. Pankaj Pawar is the CEO of Jio Platforms. KEY FINANCIALS, VALUATION Reliance Jio Platforms' revenue from operations rose 14.6% to 1.47 trillion Indian rupees ($15.45 billion) in the fiscal year ended March, while profit increased 15.1% to 300.49 billion Indian rupees. Around 90% of those figures were attributable to its telecoms business alone. MARQUEE INVESTORS In 2020, Jio Platforms raised more than $20.5 billion from 13 global investors in exchange for a roughly 33% equity stake, at a valuation range of $57 billion to $65 billion. Global names such as Meta Platforms (META.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and KKR (KKR.N) invested in the firm, as Ambani sought to turn Jio Platforms into the centerpiece of his technology ambitions. Other investors include General Atlantic, Silver Lake and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. Meta owns a 9.9% stake in the company, followed by Google's 7.7% stake. This week, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity were among investors who bid in the anchor book of the IPO, which drew more than [USN:L4N4650J2 TEXT:"$25 billion in demand"]. THE IPO JOURNEY The filing, which had been targeted for as early as March, had been pushed back as IPO activity slowed following the outbreak of the Iran war, with investors losing their appetite for new listings. The company's shares will start trading on October 28. The IPO, previously expected to be a pure offer-for-sale where foreign investors would have sold some of their holdings, will now only be a [USN:L1N41O030 TEXT:"fresh fundraising."] It has been a long road to the IPO. In 2019, Ambani said Jio would "move towards" a listing within five years, and later the plans were delayed again in 2025. The company has hired [USN:L4N4060N2 TEXT:"19 banks"] to manage its offering.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe vue sans direction, les résultats offrent un répit aux craintes en France (actualisé)
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe vue sans direction, les résultats offrent un répit aux craintes en France (actualisé) 23 octobre (Reuters) - Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sans direction vendredi à l'ouverture, bien que le CAC 40 pourrait rebondir, les résultats d'entreprise offrant un certain répit aux craintes des investisseurs sur la situation en France, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation. Kering: Le recul des ventes de Gucci au T3 pèse sur les espoirs de relance PARIS, 21 octobre (Reuters) - Le groupe de luxe français Kering a annoncé jeudi une baisse des ventes de Gucci au troisième trimestre, la faiblesse persistante de la fréquentation de ses magasins compliquant les efforts de redressement engagés par son directeur général Luca de Meo. Safran annonce des ventes en hausse de 13% au T3 PARIS, 23 octobre (Reuters) - Safran a fait état vendredi de ventes légèrement supérieures aux attentes au troisième trimestre, nourries par ses activités de construction et maintenance de moteurs. Saab: Le bénéfice dépasse les attentes au T3, porté par le réarmement STOCKHOLM, 23 octobre (Reuters) - Saab a annoncé vendredi une hausse supérieure aux attentes de son bénéfice au troisième trimestre, le groupe suédois de défense et d'aérospatiale citant une forte hausse de ses ventes, alors qu'il continue de surfer sur la vague du réarmement mondial. Electrolux: Résultat opérationnel au-dessus des attentes au T3 avec les réductions de coûts 23 octobre (Reuters) - Le fabricant suédois d'appareils électroménagers Electrolux a fait état vendredi d'un résultat opérationnel supérieur aux attentes au troisième trimestre, citant l'impact positif des économies réalisées bien que mettant en garde contre la persistance des coûts élevés liés aux matières premières et à la logistique. Eni augmente ses rachats d'actions après une hausse du bénéfice au T3 MILAN, 23 octobre (Reuters) - Eni versera un dividende exceptionnel de 1,3 milliard d'euros et augmentera légèrement son programme de rachat d'actions après avoir enregistré au troisième trimestre un bénéfice net qui a plus que doublé par rapport à l'année précédente, a annoncé vendredi le groupe énergétique. Sodexo: Le CA annuel dépasse les attentes, soutenu par les hausses de prix 23 octobre (Reuters) - Sodexo a publié vendredi un chiffre d'affaires annuel plus important que prévu, mais en léger recul de 0,5% sur un an en publié, le groupe de restauration collective citant notamment des hausses de prix d’environ 2,4%. Groupe ADP: CA en ligne au 30 septembre, Ebitda attendu dans le bas de la fourchette 22 octobre (Reuters) - Groupe ADP a affiché jeudi un chiffre d'affaires en hausse de 1,4% sur les neufs premiers mois de son exercice, en ligne avec les attentes, et a confirmé ses objectifs tout en précisant que l'Ebitda devrait se situer dans le bas de la fourchette. Volvo Cars affiche une perte au T3, prévoit la suppression de 2.500 emplois STOCKHOLM, 23 octobre (Reuters) - Volvo Cars a affiché vendredi une perte d'exploitation au troisième trimestre, impacté par la lente montée en puissance de la production de son nouveau SUV électrique EX60 et la faiblesse de la demande en Chine et aux États-Unis, et a annoncé la suppression de 2.500 emplois pour réduire ses coûts face à la concurrence chinoise. Rexel relève à nouveau ses objectifs avec les États-Unis et l'électrification en Europe 22 octobre (Reuters) - Rexel a relevé jeudi ses objectifs annuels pour la deuxième fois cette année, la forte demande des centres de données aux États-Unis et l'essor de l'électrification en Europe ayant porté les ventes trimestrielles du distributeur français de matériel électrique de 11,4% sur un an.

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: La tempête Austen balaie l'ouest de la France, 161.000 foyers privés d'électricité
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La tempête Austen balaie l'ouest de la France, 161.000 foyers privés d'électricité 23 octobre (Reuters) - Quelque 161.000 foyers étaient privés d'électricité vendredi matin dans l'ouest de la France balayé par la tempête Austen, la première de l'automne, qui s'accompagne de vents violents, rapporte Enedis. Le séisme au Tibet a fait 16 morts et 65 blessés PÉKIN, 23 octobre (Reuters) - Le séisme de magnitude 7 survenu au Tibet a fait 16 morts et 65 blessés, a annoncé vendredi le gouvernement local sur les réseaux sociaux. Manifestations au Venezuela, les premières en deux ans, pour réclamer des élections libres CARACAS, 22 octobre (Reuters) - Des milliers de Vénézuéliens sont descendus jeudi dans la rue pour réclamer la tenue d'élections libres et d'autres changements politiques, dans ce qui constitue les premières manifestations à travers le pays d'Amérique latine en près de deux ans, quelques mois après la chute de Nicolas Maduro. Brésil: Bolsonaro et Lula au coude à coude avant le second tour de la présidentielle, selon un sondage SÃO PAULO, 22 octobre (Reuters) - Le président brésilien de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro sont au coude à coude à l'approche du second tour de l'élection présidentielle qui se déroulera dimanche, montre un sondage publié jeudi par Datafolha. Les États-Unis se félicitent des progrès réalisés dans les négociations de réconciliation politique au Venezuela 22 octobre (Reuters) - Le département d'Etat américain s'est félicité jeudi de la conclusion d'un troisième cycle de négociations dans le cadre de la réconciliation politique au Venezuela. Un séisme de magnitude 7 enregistré au Tibet 22 octobre (Reuters) - Un séisme de magnitude 7 a frappé la région du Tibet, a annoncé jeudi le Centre chinois des réseaux sismiques (CENC). Brésil: Lula compte sur le vote des seniors pour l'emporter contre Bolsonaro BRASILIA, 22 octobre (Reuters) - - Rony Amaral, 71 ans, est terrifié à l'idée de voir Flavio Bolsonaro couper dans les dépenses de santé et amputer les retraites s'il l'emporte lors du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil dimanche, alors il votera pour le candidat de gauche Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, le président sortant. Le vote arabe pourrait être décisif pour évincer Netanyahu NAZARETH, Israël, 22 octobre (Reuters) - Les personnalités politiques arabo-israéliennes exhortent les électeurs de la minorité arabe à voter massivement lors des élections de la semaine prochaine afin d'évincer le Premier ministre Benjamin Netanyahu et de renverser le gouvernement le plus à droite de l'histoire du pays. Une défaite de Netanyahu changerait-elle la politique d'Israël envers les Palestiniens ? JÉRUSALEM, 22 octobre (Reuters) - Le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu et son principal rival, Gadi Eisenkot, s'opposant tous deux à la création d'un État palestinien indépendant, les élections de la semaine prochaine ont peu de chance de relancer le processus de paix quelque soit leur issue. Flavio Bolsonaro prêt, sous conditions, à divulguer ses données fiscales et financières BRASILIA, 22 octobre (Reuters) - Le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro, candidat de droite à la présidence du Brésil, a dit être prêt, sous conditions, à divulguer ses relevés bancaires, fiscaux et téléphoniques, relevant ainsi le défi posé par le président Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, son adversaire lors du second tour de la présidentielle dimanche.
